newsitem.title: CHINA: China posts $3.91 bln October trade surplus.
newsitem.headline: China posts $3.91 bln October trade surplus.

text.p: China had a trade surplus of $3.91 billion in October, the International Business Daily said on Wednesday.
This compared with a previously reported surplus of $3.2 billion in September.
This was the biggest monthly surplus of the year, fuelled by a sharp upturn in exports, the official newspaper said.
Exports in October reached $15.22 billion, up 23.3 percent over a year ago, while imports were $11.31 billion, up three percent, the daily said.
The latest figures bring the total trade surplus for the period January-October to $12.01 billion.
China's exports during the first 10 months of the year reached $119.22 billion, basically unchanged from the same period last year. Imports were $107.21 billion, up 5.5 percent from the 1995 period.

The newspaper, which is published by the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, did not give the source for the data but another official newspaper linked the trade figures to customs officials.
The newspaper said that exports, which had been sluggish for much of the year, had made a solid turnaround in recent months after hitting bottom in June.
It attributed the improvement partly to the speeded payment of export tax rebates and an expansion of credit to the nation's exporters.
The latest figures also demonstrated that domestic companies were able to deal with a host of trade barriers imposed by China's trading partners, the newspaper said.
The import data showed that the reduction of tarriffs this year was not having such a pronounced effect, it said.
